answers.can_a_sparse_exception_rescue_these_bulk: NO. Some concentration exists, but even an oracle residual at the 5% MLP-byte MATERIAL bar cannot push held-out relative L2 below 0.25. A residual large enough to carry F is no longer sparse.
answers.does_the_sensitivity_map_change_the_resi: The largest |capability − uniform| held-out L2 shift at matched byte budget is 0.000209. The map allocates the residual budget; it is not itself a byte win (licensed MLP bytes 2785280, token share 0.002802838).
answers.is_the_residual_after_the_best_bulk_spar: NO on the axes a gather-and-add exception can spend. On the best billed bulk (shared_input_r64), output-coord energy at 1% kept is 0.031056 (uniform 0.01), 50% of residual energy needs 0.438867 of the 5120 coords, W-blocks of output are dense=True, tokens need 0.315412 of rows for 50% energy. Input-direction covariance energy is concentrated (1% of dims capture 0.577492; that is ||X^T R||^2, not a measured input-sparse program). Oracle correction still needs 0.882617 of output coords to clear the 0.25 kill — not sparse.
